newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: India, Pakistan agree negotiating framework.
newsitem.headline: India, Pakistan agree negotiating framework.

text.p: Indian and Pakistani diplomats on Monday announced an agenda for future peace talks between them and a negotiating mechanism to tackle the issues.
A joint statement issued at a news conference before the departure of the Indian delegation said the agenda includes the long-standing dispute over divided Jammu and Kashmir.
The agenda, which the statement said would address "all outstanding issues of concern to both sides" covers "peace and security, including confidence-building measures".

The two countries, which have fought three wars since independence from Britain in 1947, also plan to discuss their military stand-off on the Siachen Glacier, terrorism and drug trafficking, and economic and commercial cooperation.

The statement was issued after three days of talks between delegations led by foreign ministry secretaries Shamshad Ahmad of Pakistan and Salman Haider of India, which it said had been held in a "cordial and constructive atmosphere".
"It was also agreed that both sides would take all possible steps to prevent hostile propaganda and provocative actions against each other," the statement said.
